title: Availability Continuity Certificate: Restore Proof & Scheduled DR Dry-run Validator
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Build an automated validator that produces a signed 'Availability Continuity Certificate' after each scheduled active->passive dry-run. The certificate is an auditable artifact proving snapshot immutability, checksum-matched restore, SLO gating outcomes, and circuit-breaker/load-shedding behavior under replayed traffic patterns. This ticket covers the validator harness, CI job, dashboard integration, and the Confluence template for the certificate. The validator must be runnable against both Dedicated and Private environments and emit deterministic reports that can be archived for compliance.
updates: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff: scoped acceptance criteria and identified required telemetry (latency p50/p90/p99, success rate, KV-consistency hashes, snapshot IDs). Attendees: Avery C., Maya P., Jonah Ruiz (SRE), Priya K. (Security).

2026-02-18 - Prototype: initial checksum verifier implemented in dr-tools repo. Command-line proof-of-concept can mount a snapshot, compute per-shard SHA256, and compare with recorded manifest. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dr-tools/pull/314
2026-02-25 - Telemetry hooks added: runtime now emits 'restore.fidelity' events and 'prefix-kv-drift' metrics. Dashboards updated (see artifacts).

2026-03-01 - Circuit breaker simulation: added synthetic failures to validate CB hysteresis thresholds and emergency load-shedding rules. Simulation results show graceful degradation under 3x baseline qps when KV warmup disabled.

2026-03-05 - Integration test: ran a scheduled dry-run on staging-us-west-2 with canary traffic replay. RTO measured = 4m32s, snapshot verification passed, but p99 latency spike to 420ms during warmup — flagged for batching/priority warmup. See notes for mitigation steps.

2026-03-09 - Security review stubbed: Priya K. completed threat surface analysis for certificate signing keys, recommended KMS usage and HSM-backed signing. Action: add key rotation doc to Confluence.

2026-03-12 - Validator CI job created: nightly job that runs against isolated sandbox and uploads certificate to S3 and Confluence page. Job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-ci/actions/runs/72611
acceptance_criteria: Automated dry-run validator produces a signed PDF certificate plus machine-readable JSON report and pushes both to S3/Confluence.
Certificate includes: snapshot_id, per-shard SHA256 list, restore RTO/RPO, SLO results (success rate, p50/p90/p99 latencies), circuit-breaker activations, and applied load-shedding policy.
Restore verification must detect any checksum mismatch and mark certificate as FAILED with root-cause hints.
Nightly CI job runs without human intervention and archives 90 days of certificates in the compliance bucket.
Dashboard tile shows most recent certificate status and links to historical certificates; alert on FAILED certificates routed to pager duty for SRE on-call.
Signed keys are stored in KMS; signing operation requires two-step approval for production certificate rotation (documented).
risks: Warmup latency during KV rehydration can produce transient SLO violations; mitigations required: warm-priority-traffic, gradual concurrency ramp, and pre-warmed snapshot replicas.
If certificate signing key is compromised, historical certificates could be forged — enforced KMS/HSM usage and enforced rotation needed.
Nightly dry-runs consume Dedicated capacity; must be scheduled to avoid contention with customer-scheduled bursts (policy required).
notes: Follow-up: pair with runtime team to experiment with continuous prefix caching during restore to reduce p99 warmup spikes.
Consider adding a low-cost 'snapshot smoke' job that validates immutability immediately after snapshot creation to catch corruption earlier.
Long-term: extend certificate to include reproducibility hashes for deterministic restore (random seeds, runtime versions).
